A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CURSOR study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original EEG-based ranking and optimization results, ablations, alternative EEG representations and human perceptual studies, including H-ID with 53 participants.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds retrieval metrics and analyses of CURSOR score variability.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same hypothesis-specific regression, shuffled-data comparison and RMSE-ratio score. Ranking and optimization procedures remain unchanged. Alternative losses and persistent estimators are discussed as possibilities, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic-face EEG data, 17 target faces, 170 simulated datasets, ranking and optimization tasks, EEGNet training data and human studies. The added retrieval and stability analyses introduce no new population, domain or test environment.

E2.justification: Section 7 adds a numerical, literature-based comparison with the supervised decoder of de la Torre-Ortiz and Ruotsalo: RMSE 0.17 ± 0.09 versus CURSOR's retained 0.18 ± 0.08. This is contextual comparison with acknowledged cross-validation differences, not a documented rerun. The evaluated comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 reports a second-order solver where v1 specified gradient descent for constructing simulated stimuli. Appendix A changes the stated trial and target counts from 16 to 17 while retaining 1,120 images; neither revision establishes rerunning experiments. Appendix E.4 adds top-k, minimum-distance-at-top-k and SNR-like evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.4 examines score sensitivity to folds, random splits and dataset size through score dispersion and signal-to-noise analyses. This focused robustness addition supplements the unchanged dimensionality, estimator, data-scarcity and near-target ablations.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports uncertainty of CURSOR scores directly across folds and splits, including standard deviations relative to means and an SNR-like summary. The existing ten-fold procedure, result error bars, confidence intervals and significance tests remain. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the main optimization results retain their values. New Tables 3–4 report additional retrieval outcomes, including LR top-10 accuracy of 0.800 versus Random's 0.155 and minimum top-10 distance of 0.176 versus 4.194. Figures 10–12 add score-variability and SNR findings, rather than improvements to previously reported performance.

T1.justification: Appendix E.4 introduces a mathematical definition of an SNR-like statistic: the standard deviation of per-hypothesis mean scores divided by mean within-hypothesis standard deviation. The core self-calibration equations and assumptions are unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: a first continuous-domain self-calibrating BCI framework, label-free target ranking and recovery, perceptually similar generated targets, and a released dataset. Added explanations and evidence do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability boundaries and interpretation. It explicitly distinguishes offline iteration from closed-loop operation, explains acquisition bias, and acknowledges that selecting PCA dimensions used ground-truth metrics unavailable in deployment. Appendix F adds real-face and model limitations and concrete privacy considerations; Appendix E.4 links MLP's weaker retrieval to score variability.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit project and code/data access links, details diagonal latent-space sampling and within-window EEG averaging, and specifies that aligned and shuffled errors use identical held-out folds. Existing hardware and hyperparameter documentation is retained. The links provide access instructions; their availability is not verified by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens supporting literature on face perception and psychometric sampling, dimensionality reduction and optimization, and cognitive privacy, consent and data governance. It also explicitly positions the offline study relative to closed-loop face retrieval. The original BCI literature and central novelty claim remain.

P1.justification: V2 substantially expands explanations of self-calibration, acquisition, simulation construction, cross-validation and calibration recovery. It reorganizes the brief limitations appendix into a structured discussion, moves references before the appendices, and adds acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist while retaining the main section framework.

P2.justification: Appendix visual reporting expands with two retrieval tables and three score-stability/SNR figures. V1 Figures 8 and 9 are combined as v2 Figure 8a–b, and other displays are relocated. The principal existing figures and tables retain their scientific content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through clearer implementation details, explicit access links and more candid limits on offline evaluation and ground-truth-dependent dimension selection. The new stability analyses help assess the scoring mechanism without changing the main results. These gains are limited by unresolved reporting issues, including Appendix A's 17 trials of 70 images but unchanged total of 1,120.
